decision.question: Which architecture best prevents stale-badge bugs in a three-class notification system?

caveats: Badge stays stale if list mutates outside tray.add()
Reuses .on() for custom events, one more concept to learn

options.text: Notice dismisses itself, tray reads DOM
caveats: Badge stays stale if list mutates outside tray.notify()

decision.why: Option B is the only choice where the stale-badge bug is structurally impossible. The event fires from the one place data changes, so any caller sees the update. Options A and C both require discipline—remembering to call an update line—which breaks in production. The cost is low: .on() already exists for clicks, so this reuses a familiar pattern.
